newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI cuts prime rate to 14.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI cuts prime rate to 14.5 pct.

text.p: India's largest commercial bank, the State Bank of India (SBI), on Thursday said it would cut its prime lending rate (PLR) to 14.5 percent from 15.5 percent with effect from November 1.

The bank said it was reducing the maximum spread over PLR to 3.75 percent from 4.5 percent. SBI's board of directors also decided to cut the interest rate on term deposits upto a maximum of one percentage point.
The interest on term deposits have been cut as follows:
- From 30 days to 45 days, to 7.0 percent a year from 8.0 percent earlier, from 46 days to 179 days to 8.5 percent from 9.0 percent.

- Interest on deposits over 180 days to one year would be unchanged at 10 percent, above one year and upto two years unchanged at 11.0 percent, and over two years and upto three years unchanged at 12 percent.
- Deposits over three years would attract a reduced interest rate of 12.5 percent per annum, down from 13.0 percent.

- Interest on NRE (non-resident Indian external account) deposits of over six months upto two years would be unchanged at 12 percent. Interest on NRE deposits of over two years would be cut to 14.0 percent from 15.0 percent.
NRNR (non-resident non-repatriable) deposits above six months and upto three years would be cut to 16.0 percent from 17.0 percent.
